tickets.title: US001 (Student)
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to search for available courses by keyword, so that I can quickly find classes that match my interests.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given a keyword, the system returns a list of courses containing that keyword in title or description.
- Search results must display course name, code, and schedule.
- If no courses match, the system shows “No results found.”

tickets.title: US002 (Student)
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to drag and drop courses into my calendar, so that I can visualize my weekly schedule.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Dragging a course into the calendar displays its time slot.
- If a conflict exists, the system highlights the overlap in red.
- Removing a course from the calendar clears its time slot.

tickets.title: US003 (Student)
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to filter courses by prerequisites, so that I only see classes I am eligible to enroll in.
Acceptance Criteria:
-Filter option hides courses where prerequisites are not met.
-Eligible courses remain visible.
-The filter can be toggled on or off.

analysis.ambiguity1:
Requirement: “The kitchen needs a screen that shows orders as they come in.”
Why vague: The requirement does not specify how detailed the order display should be. It is unclear whether the screen must show only item names, preparation instructions, or customer details. Without clarification, developers cannot design the kitchen interface properly.
analysis.ambiguity2: Requirement: “The app should send push notifications to students at 11:30 AM offering them a discount on the daily special.” Why vague: The requirement does not define how discounts are calculated or applied. It is unclear whether the discount is a fixed percentage, a fixed amount, or varies by item. Without clarification, developers cannot implement the notification and pricing logic correctly.
analysis.conflictSolution:
Conflict: The Cafeteria Manager wants mobile ordering to reduce queues, but the IT Infrastructure Team highlights unreliable Wi-Fi in the basement, which could disrupt the kitchen display system.
Resolution: The app will support offline caching for at least 10 minutes. Orders placed during outages will be stored locally and synced once the connection is restored. This ensures mobile ordering works smoothly while addressing infrastructure concerns.
analysis.nfr1: Usability: The menu filter must allow students with allergies to hide unsafe items completely, reducing stress and improving user experience.
analysis.nfr2: Performance: The system must update the kitchen display within two seconds of receiving a new order.
analysis.nfr3: Reliability: The kitchen display must continue to function offline for at least 10 minutes and sync seamlessly once the internet is restored.
